trigger.summary: Repeated volume and cache acceptance failures required diagnosis of intent, writer grant and crash-released coordinator ownership. Clean-environment CI then required fixture canonicalization and failure-only terminal observability before further cleanup changes.
trigger.root_cause: Pre-admission intents were conflated with already-issued debt, and original/recovery paths granted writer independently. Cache identity was initially uncommitted across the held operation; later contention was treated as fatal before mutex acquisition, while the recovery fixture incorrectly expected one-shot admission.

recommendation.reason: After diagnosis use intent -> reservation -> one atomic local grant CAS. Preserve conservative unknown delivery and all owner/resource fences. Independent review and real process scenarios must pass before release. Cache gate diagnosis found valid dead coordinator pid13976 leaving a global gate; approved double-mutex transition preserves old-client wx barrier, records rather than erases mutex evidence, and leaves every resource guard unchanged. Cache delta keeps identity durable before grant, performs validation under the held mutex, maps normal contention to retryable busy, and captures both child outcomes before teardown. Required regression checks remain pending until executed. Realtime input normalization and separate missing-editor diagnostics are a bounded repair of an observed false Stop, preserving existing book/review requirements and old request evidence.
recommendation.rejected_alternative: Removing gates hides incomplete work and compromises resource safety; keeping project-only admission cannot satisfy the approved concurrent-project scenario.
